phase04aFinalRepairRevisionNote: Phase 04A FINAL REPAIR (2026-09-21, Sky's D-04A-2 decision, after a fresh independent Opus acceptance review held the rev-7 repair as a real defect): rev 7's deleteFlag ordering fix (cleanup PROVEN before the row DELETE) rested on treating a Storage remove() call's `error: null` response as proof the object was actually gone. The review established that is not proof under the flag-photos Storage policies this client can see — a refused or no-op removal can return an empty deleted-object list with no error, so deleteFlag could still delete the row while the public photo stayed live. The fix is not more client-side cleanup logic; it is refusing to claim proof the client cannot obtain. deleteFlag now refuses outright — no Storage call, no row DELETE — for ANY flag with a photo (primary or gallery, resolvable or not); only a zero-photo flag still deletes via the direct-DELETE path. Separately, FDA-019's legacy uid-folder Storage upload fallback (mirroring uploadAvatar's) is no longer used for NEW signed-in flag photos: it has no server-side hold protecting the object the way an upload intent does, so when the upload-intent RPC is absent, photo attachment is gated (FlagPhotoAttachmentUnavailableError) instead of writing an unrecoverable public object. Report submission without a photo, and the avatar surface's own legacy fallback, are both unaffected. See qa-reports/phase04/04A-final-repair-20260921T214936Z/HANDOFF.md.
phase04aRepairRevisionNote: Phase 04A REPAIR (2026-09-21, after an independent Opus acceptance HOLD on 6b239dd found two real defects): (1) FDA-002 deleteFlag's ordering was inverted — it deleted the flags row first and cleaned up photos best-effort afterward, so a Storage failure could leave a public photo orphaned with the row already gone (the exact SR-050 takedown risk). Per Sky's D-04A-1 decision, required photo cleanup now happens BEFORE the row DELETE and is fail-closed: a Storage error, or a photo whose exact object path cannot be established (no owner uid to validate against, a foreign folder, a malformed URL), now REFUSES the delete instead of proceeding. Nothing in this repair is 'best-effort' any more — every photo this flag's rows reference must be provably removed or the row survives. (2) FDA-019's batchInsertFlagPhotos only cleaned up the ONE photo whose row-insert failed; every already-uploaded photo after it in the batch (never even attempted) was left orphaned in Storage with no DB pointer. batchInsertFlagPhotos now cleans up every unattached photo — the failing one and everything after it — on any failure, leaving already-attached photos untouched. contractManifest.guard.test.ts's FDA-002/FDA-019 sub-tests and the D1F4R3 source-closure/replay guards were updated in the same repair to assert the accepted current contract instead of the pre-04A one; see 04A-repair HANDOFF for the full predicate list.

No Phase03A/03B RPC-dependent surface (flag-status-transition, leaderboard) or FDA-003 (account-deletion, owned by 04B) changed. revisionNote: Rev 2 corrects rev 1 after independent review. Rev 1 was accurate at NAME granularity but wrong at CALL-SITE granularity: it omitted a call site, misattributed two files, classified four sites by the throw at the call rather than by what the caller does with it, and did not record the moderation-column WRITE sites at all. Classifications below are per call site and were each read at the cited line.

onAbsentDefinitions.hard: the call throws AND a user-visible action fails
onAbsentDefinitions.degraded: the call throws but the caller completes the primary action and tells the user what was lost
onAbsentDefinitions.graceful: absence is detected and a working alternative path or empty state is used
onAbsentDefinitions.swallowed: the error is caught and discarded; no user-visible effect
onAbsentDefinitions.silent: no error check at all — the failure is invisible to code and user alike
onAbsentDefinitions.unreachable: cannot be called when its prerequisite contract is absent
onAbsentDefinitions.fail_closed: the capability is withheld with a warning and no permissive fallback
onAbsentDefinitions.optional_omitted: the call fails but successfully loaded primary content remains visible while optional dependent content is omitted

surfaces.phase04aNote: Phase 04A (2026-09-21): uploadFlagPhoto now mirrors uploadAvatar's isFunctionMissing fallback exactly — prepare_flag_photo_upload absence is detected and the proven pre-intent uid-folder Storage path is used instead, with a direct flag_photos row insert (photos.ts insertLegacyFlagPhoto) replacing the commit RPC. The upload-intent path is unchanged and still used when the RPCs are present. SUPERSEDED by phase04aFinalRepairNote below — this legacy fallback is no longer taken for new signed-in flag photos.
surfaces.phase04aRepairNote: Phase 04A REPAIR (2026-09-21): independent review found the legacy fallback above could orphan Storage objects on a multi-photo submit — batchInsertFlagPhotos (photos.ts) only cleaned up the ONE photo whose flag_photos row-insert failed; every already-uploaded photo AFTER it in the same batch (never even attempted) was left as a real object in the flag-photos bucket with no DB row pointing at it, for any batch mixing intent-based and legacy uploads. Repaired: on any attach failure, every not-yet-attached photo from that point on is now cleaned up too (cancelFlagPhotoUpload for intent-based uploads, removeUploadedFlagPhotos for legacy ones) — already-attached photos before the failure are left untouched. See src/lib/__tests__/photos.test.ts's 'FDA-019 orphan repair' suite (failure at first/middle/final position, mixed intent+legacy) for the behavioral proof. Still true and unaffected by phase04aFinalRepairNote below (batchInsertFlagPhotos itself is unchanged) — it now simply has no reachable legacy-branch input for a brand-new flag photo.
surfaces.phase04aFinalRepairNote: Phase 04A FINAL REPAIR (2026-09-21, Sky's D-04A-2 decision): the legacy uid-folder Storage upload fallback above has no server-side hold protecting the object the way an upload intent does — if the flag_photos row insert that must follow it never happens or fails ambiguously, the only cleanup is client best-effort, and a public object can be left with no DB row pointing at it. That trade-off was held unacceptable for a BRAND NEW signed-in photo. uploadFlagPhoto (flags.ts) now throws FlagPhotoAttachmentUnavailableError as soon as prepare_flag_photo_upload's absence is detected, BEFORE buildPath returns a path and therefore before uploadStrippedImage's own supabase.storage.upload() call — no Storage object is ever written. photo attachment is gated; ordinary report submission without a photo, and the avatar surface's own separate legacy fallback (users.ts, untouched by this decision), are both unaffected. See src/lib/__tests__/flags.test.ts's 'uploadFlagPhoto — FDA-019 gated when the upload-intent RPC is absent (D-04A-2)' suite.

surfaces.phase04aNote: Phase 04A (2026-09-21): deleteFlag no longer calls the undeployed delete-flag Edge Function (P04-D01, accepted 2026-09-03 — do not deploy D1F4 merely to satisfy the client). It now issues a strict direct Data API DELETE authorized entirely by the live RLS below, requires a returned id (zero rows = FlagDeleteRefusedError, never a silent/false success). surfaces.phase04aRepairNote: Phase 04A REPAIR (2026-09-21, Sky's D-04A-1 decision): required photo cleanup happened BEFORE the row DELETE and failed closed on any problem, by calling storage.remove() on every required object and treating error:null as proof of removal before issuing the flags DELETE. SUPERSEDED by phase04aFinalRepairNote below — a fresh independent review held that storage.remove()'s error:null response is NOT proof of removal (a refused/no-op delete can return an empty deleted-object list with no error), so this ordering could still delete the row while a public photo stayed live. Do not reintroduce a client-side Storage cleanup step before the flags DELETE on the strength of this note; it describes a superseded, unsafe behavior kept here only as history.
surfaces.phase04aFinalRepairNote: Phase 04A FINAL REPAIR (2026-09-21, Sky's D-04A-2 decision): deleteFlag no longer attempts ANY client-side Storage cleanup. It refuses the delete outright (FlagPhotoCleanupUnprovenError) for a flag with any photo — primary or gallery, exact object_key or legacy url, resolvable or not — leaving both the row and every photo exactly as they were, with no supabase.storage call made at all. Only a flag with zero photos reaches the direct flags DELETE (unchanged from the phase04aNote description: RETURNING id, intended-id validated, zero/wrong-id refuses). This is a stricter, simpler compatibility behavior than the repair note above: it trades an anonymous flag's (or any flag's) photo-bearing report becoming client-undeletable until an accepted backend capability can prove exact Storage removal, for the guarantee that this client can never report a false deletion success while a public photo remains reachable. The 2026-09-04 deployed-contract.v1.json capture's RLS/policy confirmations ('flags delete own', 'admin delete any flag') remain accurate and unaffected — only the client's own required-cleanup logic changed. See src/lib/__tests__/flags.supabase.test.ts's 'deleteFlag' describe block and src/__tests__/d1f4r3SourceClosure.guard.test.ts's D-04A-2 source-order guard.
